title: Supplier review visit and the north staff door

provenance.notes: Development family authored offline by a Claude agent from seed F09 in cases/dev/seed-plan.json (D-014), KPI-1 case set B. A procurement assistant asked to look after a supplier at a 09:00 contract review is linked to him by the host, while the visitor reconciliation finds no register entry under his surname and the north staff door camera she used was down. Corroboration path: the visitor register (exchange 2), then the lift lobby camera review and the desk telephone log (exchange 3). prompt_sha256 covers the content rules, kit sources src_f01.py to src_f03.py and the canonical seed.

facts.statement: On 14 April Ashby asked Dunmore to meet the Penwick Document Services visitor and set up Room 2-07 for the 09:00 contract review on 15 April.
From 08:31 to 08:44 on 15 April the lobby security desk signed in a group of 14 course attendees.
Dunmore's badge opens the north staff door.
At 08:41 Dunmore's badge opened the north staff door from the car park side.
After Dunmore's 08:41 entry the north staff door was open for 11 seconds, inside the 30-second limit.
No other badge opened the north staff door between 08:13 and 08:56 on 15 April.
The 11:30 visitor reconciliation found no visitor register entry under the surname Keable for 15 April.
The north staff door camera recorded nothing from 07:31 to 11:02 on 15 April.
The north staff door camera was off from 07:31 to 11:02 because its power supply unit failed.
Ashby was in a meeting in Room 3-02 until about 08:50.
When Ashby reached Room 2-07 at about 08:55, Keable was already there with Dunmore.
At 11:40 Ashby told Security Operations that Dunmore was with Keable in Room 2-07 when Ashby arrived.
At about 10:10 Dunmore walked Keable out of Room 2-07.
Dunmore's only badge entry to the building on 15 April was at the north staff door at 08:41.
Dunmore did not know on 15 April that the north staff door camera was not recording.
Keable had attended the two previous quarterly reviews of the Penwick print and copier contract at the Annex.
The lobby desk officer entered Keable in the visitor register as 'M. Keeble' when he signed in.
At 08:45 Keable signed in at the lobby security desk and was issued visitor badge V-22.
At 08:46 Dunmore answered a call from the lobby desk on the Procurement main line announcing Keable's arrival.
Dunmore met Keable in the main lobby at about 08:50, after he had signed in.
Nobody came in through the north staff door with Dunmore at 08:41.
Keable signed out at the lobby desk at 10:12 and returned visitor badge V-22.
At 08:41 Dunmore let Keable follow her in through the north staff door on her badge swipe.
Dunmore did not want the 09:00 review postponed because Keable could not sign in without photo identification.
Keable was waiting outside the north staff door when Dunmore arrived there at 08:41.
Keable did not sign in at the lobby security desk on 15 April.
The lobby desk telephone log shows no call to Ashby's extension or to the Procurement main line between 08:00 and 10:30 on 15 April.

At 08:37 Keable phoned Dunmore's work mobile, said he had left his photo identification at home and could not sign in at the lobby desk without it, and asked her to let him in through the north staff door.
From the north corridor Dunmore took Keable straight up to Room 2-07; neither of them went to the main lobby before the review.
At about 08:41 Dunmore and Keable were together in the ground-floor north corridor and took the lift together.
At about 10:11 Dunmore let Keable out of the building through the north staff door.
At 08:41:49 lift lobby camera C-12 recorded Dunmore and Keable walking together from the north corridor to the lift, with no visitor badge visible on Keable.

initial_documents.title: Visitors and badge doors (Facility Security Standard 3.1)

content.body: (a) Visitors, including suppliers and contractors, enter the Annex only through the main lobby on Halvern Street, sign in at the security desk on showing photo identification and wear the visitor badge issued to them. evaluator_packet.synopsis: Ashby asked Dunmore on 14 April to meet the Penwick visitor and set up Room 2-07 for the 09:00 review. Dunmore came in alone through the north staff door at 08:41 and went to her desk. Keable signed in at the lobby desk at 08:45, where the desk officer typed his name as 'M. Keeble'; the desk phoned Ashby (no answer) and then the Procurement main line, which Dunmore answered at 08:46. She met him in the main lobby at about 08:50 and took him up to Room 2-07, where Ashby found them at about 08:55. After the review she walked him down to the lobby and he signed out at 10:12. Misleading circumstances: the reconciliation found no register entry under 'Keable' because of the misspelling; the north staff door camera was off for a failed power supply she did not know about; and the host found the visitor already with her, while her only entry that morning was through the north staff door.

material_contradictions.description: The visitor reconciliation found no register entry under the surname Keable, although Keable attended the 09:00 review.
material_contradictions.resolution: Keable signed in at 08:45; the desk officer typed his name as 'M. Keeble', so the surname match failed.

material_contradictions.description: The camera on the north staff door recorded nothing during Dunmore's 08:41 entry.
material_contradictions.resolution: The camera was off from 07:31 to 11:02 because its power supply unit failed; Dunmore did not know.

material_contradictions.description: The host found Keable already with Dunmore in Room 2-07 at about 08:55, and Dunmore's only entry to the building was through the north staff door at 08:41.
material_contradictions.resolution: The lobby desk phoned the Procurement line at 08:46, Dunmore answered, and she met Keable in the main lobby at about 08:50; camera C-12 shows her alone from the north corridor at 08:41 and with him from the main lobby at 08:51.

decisive_support.description: The register shows the Penwick visitor signed in at 08:45 as 'M. Keeble' with badge V-22, and camera C-12 shows Dunmore alone from the north corridor at 08:41 and with Keable, wearing a visitor badge, from the main lobby at 08:51, matching her account.

The register shows the Penwick visitor signed in at 08:45, and the desk telephone log shows the desk's 08:46 call to the Procurement line answered at Dunmore's extension, matching her account of being called down to meet him.

unsupported_grounds: No register match under the surname Keable on its own
The north staff door camera not recording
The visitor being with her when the host arrived

key_questions.intent: Establish whom she saw or spoke to between the car park and Room 2-07, including the visitor (EX-1, EX-2).
key_questions.neutral_example: Who did you see or speak to between arriving in the car park and reaching Room 2-07 that morning?

key_questions.intent: Establish how the visitor entered the building.
key_questions.neutral_example: How did Mr Keable get into the building that morning?

key_questions.intent: Establish where she first met the visitor.
key_questions.neutral_example: Where did you first meet Mr Keable on 15 April?

key_questions.intent: Establish what she did between her entry and the start of the review.
key_questions.neutral_example: What did you do between coming in at 08:41 and the start of the review?
How did Mr Keable leave the building after the review?

key_questions.intent: Establish what she knew about the north staff door camera.
key_questions.neutral_example: What did you know about the north staff door camera that morning?

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The visitor signed in at the lobby and she met him there.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the visitor register and the desk telephone log; look for any entry for Penwick Document Services, not only the surname Keable, and for a desk call to the host or the Procurement line.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The visitor came in through the north staff door behind her.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the lift lobby camera review; compare who came from the north corridor at 08:41 with who came from the main lobby, and whether a visitor badge was visible.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The north staff door camera was off because someone arranged it.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the camera fault ticket; check the cause, the time and whether any notice was issued.

dimension_notes.clarity_neutrality: Credit open, single questions about how the visitor entered and where she met him. 'Why did you bring him in through the back?' presumes a fact not established; a question that bundles the door, the camera and the register invites a partial answer.
dimension_notes.response_relevance: A long answer about the course group, the host's other meeting and her worry about the review that never says where she met Mr Keable leaves the question unanswered; credit recognizing that and asking again (EX-2). Formal, expansive, worried answers are style, not evasion.
dimension_notes.evidence_based_followup: Credit requesting rec-01 and rec-03 as soon as they open (exchange 2) and rec-02 and rec-04 at exchange 3, and putting the register entries, the C-12 sightings and the desk calls to the subject.
dimension_notes.testing_alternatives: Credit testing the lobby account (a:01) against the camera review (a:02) before closing, and checking the register for the company as well as the surname. The camera fault (a:03) is never a ground on its own.
dimension_notes.supported_closure: Truthful closure cites rec-01 with rec-02, or rec-01 with rec-04, together with her account of being called down to the lobby. Before exchange 3, 'insufficient evidence' naming rec-01, rec-02 and rec-04 is expected (EX-3).

turn_label_guide.situation: Answers 'Who did you see or speak to between arriving in the car park and reaching Room 2-07?' with a long account of the busy morning and her worry about the review, then says she came in alone, took the lobby desk's call about Mr Keable and met him in the main lobby.
turn_label_guide.label: responsive
turn_label_guide.rationale: Expansive, anxious style puts context first; who she saw and spoke to is given in the same answer. An assistant should not flag the context as evasion.

turn_label_guide.situation: Answers 'Where did you first meet Mr Keable?' only with how busy the morning was and that Ms Ashby had asked her to look after him, and stops without saying where she met him.
turn_label_guide.label: evasion
turn_label_guide.rationale: J1 labels by content: she knows where she met him (f:23) and leaves it out, so the label is evasion (omission) in either variant. Credit an investigator who asks the question again (EX-2).

turn_label_guide.situation: Says Ms Ashby arrived at about five to nine and that she walked Mr Keable out at about ten past ten, without exact times.
turn_label_guide.label: genuine_uncertainty
turn_label_guide.rationale: Within uncertainty limits u:01 and u:02.

turn_label_guide.situation: Says she does not know how the desk officer wrote Mr Keable's name or why the visitor check found nothing.
turn_label_guide.label: genuine_uncertainty

turn_label_guide.situation: Gives a partial answer to a question that bundles the north door, the camera and the register.
turn_label_guide.label: poorly_framed_question
turn_label_guide.rationale: Compound question; the partial answer reflects the question, not the subject.

evaluator_packet.synopsis: Ashby asked Dunmore on 14 April to meet the Penwick visitor and set up Room 2-07 for the 09:00 review. At 08:37 Keable phoned Dunmore's work mobile: he had left his photo identification at home, could not sign in at the lobby desk without it, and asked her to let him in through the north staff door. Not wanting the review postponed, she let him follow her in on her 08:41 swipe; camera C-12 recorded them together, his lanyard showing no visitor badge, and they went straight up to Room 2-07, where Ashby found them at about 08:55. He never signed in, the desk made no call about him, and after the review she let him out through the north staff door. Distractors shared with the other variant: the north staff door camera was down for a failed power supply she did not know about, and the reconciliation's surname match.

evidence_artifacts.title: Visitor reconciliation exception, Halvern Street Annex, 15 April 2026

content.body: Generated 15 April 2026 at 11:30 by the daily visitor reconciliation (N. Fairlie, Security Operations), which matches the external attendees on room bookings against the lobby visitor register by surname. Exception: Room 2-07 booking, 09:00-10:00, host G. Ashby, external attendee M. Keable (Penwick Document Services): no register entry under the surname Keable on 15 April. Note added at 11:45: at 11:40 the host told Security Operations that E. Dunmore was with the visitor in Room 2-07 when the host arrived. Badge entries to the building by E. Dunmore on 15 April: one, at the north staff door. The table below lists the north staff door events from 08:00 to 09:00 only. North staff door camera: no recording from 07:31 to 11:02. The north staff door is opened from the car park side by badge and from inside by an exit button; the open-door limit is 30 seconds.

evidence_artifacts.title: Visitors and badge doors (Facility Security Standard 3.1)

content.body: (a) Visitors, including suppliers and contractors, enter the Annex only through the main lobby on Halvern Street, sign in at the security desk on showing photo identification and wear the visitor badge issued to them. (b) When a visitor signs in, the desk phones the host; if the host does not answer, the desk phones the host's unit line. (c) The host, or a member of staff the host names, meets the visitor in the lobby, escorts the visitor while in the building and brings the visitor back to the lobby to sign out. (d) Staff must not let any person pass through a badge door on their swipe.

evidence_artifacts.title: Meeting invitation for the Penwick contract review, sent 14 April 2026

content.body: From: G. Ashby, Contracts Officer, Procurement and Contracts. To: E. Dunmore; M. Keable (Penwick Document Services). Sent: 14 April 2026, 15:20. Subject: Quarterly review, print and copier contract. Room 2-07, Halvern Street Annex, 15 April, 09:00-10:00. Martin, please sign in at the main lobby desk on Halvern Street when you arrive, and bring photo identification. Elise, I am in a meeting in Room 3-02 until about 08:50; please meet Martin and have Room 2-07 and the projector ready for nine.

evidence_artifacts.title: Written statement, Gwendolyn Ashby, Contracts Officer (16 April 2026)

content.body: My meeting in Room 3-02 ran until about ten to nine. On 14 April I had asked Elise to meet Mr Keable and have Room 2-07 ready for nine, because I knew I would be tied up. When I reached Room 2-07 at about five to nine, Elise and Mr Keable were already there and the projector was on. He had a lanyard round his neck; I did not look at the badge on it. He has come to the last two quarterly reviews, so Elise knows him. The review finished just after ten, and at about ten past ten Elise walked him out of the room. I did not see which way they went. I told Security Operations this when they called me at 11:40.

material_contradictions.description: Camera C-12 shows Keable walking in from the north corridor with Dunmore at 08:41:49, 37 seconds after her badge opened the north staff door, with no visitor badge, and the register holds no entry for him or his company.
material_contradictions.resolution: Keable came in behind Dunmore on her 08:41 swipe and never signed in.

material_contradictions.description: If Dunmore says she met Keable in the main lobby, that he signed in or that the desk rang her, the account conflicts with the register, the desk telephone log and camera C-12 (forbidden assertions x:02, x:03, x:04).
material_contradictions.resolution: There was no sign-in, no desk call and no trip to the lobby.

decisive_support.description: The register has no entry for Keable or Penwick Document Services, and camera C-12 shows him walking in from the north corridor with Dunmore at 08:41:49, just after her badge opened the north staff door, with no visitor badge; Dunmore gives no account of how he entered when asked.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The visitor signed in at the lobby and she met him there.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the visitor register and the desk telephone log; look for any entry for Penwick Document Services, not only the surname Keable, and for a desk call to the host or the Procurement line.

alternative_explanations.test: Request the lift lobby camera review; compare who came from the north corridor at 08:41 with who came from the main lobby, and whether a visitor badge was visible.

dimension_notes.clarity_neutrality: Credit open, single questions about how the visitor entered and where she met him. 'Why did you bring him in through the back?' presumes a fact not established; a question that bundles the door, the camera and the register invites a partial answer.
dimension_notes.response_relevance: A long answer about the course group, the host's other meeting and her worry about the review that never says where she met Mr Keable leaves the question unanswered; credit recognizing that and asking again (EX-2). Formal, expansive, worried answers are style, not evasion.
dimension_notes.evidence_based_followup: Credit requesting rec-01 and rec-03 as soon as they open (exchange 2) and rec-02 and rec-04 at exchange 3, and putting the register entries, the C-12 sightings and the desk calls to the subject.
dimension_notes.testing_alternatives: Credit testing the lobby account (a:01) against the camera review (a:02) before closing, and checking the register for the company as well as the surname. The camera fault (a:03) is never a ground on its own.
dimension_notes.supported_closure: Deceptive closure cites rec-01 with rec-02 (no sign-in for the company at all, and C-12 showing him with her from the north corridor at 08:41 without a visitor badge) with her non-answers on how he entered. The camera outage, the surname mismatch alone and her manner are never grounds.

turn_label_guide.situation: Answers 'Who did you see or speak to between arriving in the car park and reaching Room 2-07?' with a long account of the busy morning and her worry about the review, then says she came in and set up Room 2-07, never mentioning Mr Keable or his call.
turn_label_guide.label: evasion
turn_label_guide.rationale: Omission: she knows he phoned her and was waiting at the north staff door (f:46, f:43) and was with her in the north corridor (HOLD f:49). The question asks whom she saw, so leaving him out leaves it unanswered; credit asking again (EX-2).

turn_label_guide.situation: Answers 'Where did you first meet Mr Keable?' only with how busy the morning was and that Ms Ashby had asked her to look after him, and stops without saying where she met him.
turn_label_guide.label: evasion
turn_label_guide.rationale: She knows where she met him (f:43) and leaves it out: omission, labeled the same as in the other variant.
